name: World News
description: A general international briefing for anyone who wants the day's major stories without a single outlet's framing. Deliberately spreads across British, American, European, Asian and Middle Eastern newsrooms.

themes.label: Conflict & Security
themes.hint: Armed violence and the threat of it: battlefield developments, strikes and casualties, ceasefires and hostage talks, insurgency and terrorism, arms transfers, and military posturing between states.

themes.label: Diplomacy & Institutions
themes.hint: States negotiating rather than fighting: summits and state visits, treaties, sanctions and their relief, UN, NATO, EU and G20 proceedings, international court cases, and ambassadorial or recognition disputes.

themes.label: Domestic Politics
themes.hint: Power inside one country: elections and results, coalition formation and no confidence votes, protests and crackdowns, coups, corruption scandals and leadership changes. The story stops at the border.

themes.label: Economy & Trade
themes.hint: Cross border economics: tariffs and trade deals, central bank decisions and currency crises, energy and commodity prices, debt restructuring and IMF programmes, supply chains and multinational operations.

themes.label: Disasters & Health
themes.hint: Sudden harm from nature or systems failure: earthquakes, floods, storms and wildfires, famine and displacement, outbreaks and public health emergencies, industrial and transport accidents, and the relief response.

themes.label: Society & Rights
themes.hint: People and norms rather than states: migration and asylum, press freedom and censorship, religious and ethnic tension, gender and labour rights, courts ruling on civil liberties, and cultural flashpoints.
